messages:
pagerduty-bot: Pager: SEV=page - edge-us-west serving cluster high packet loss + 1+ CUDA OOMs across 3 nodes. Trigger: rdma_rx_err rate > 100/min, client 5xx spike. Escalation path: eng-oncall -> eng-sre. Link: https://ops.internal/incidents/2934012000

Dave_oncall: acked. grabbing context. Anyone oncall for edge-us-west networking? :eyes:

Alice_sre: I'm here. seeing large retransmit counters on ib0, RX drops, and gdr resets. Affected pods: serve-v2-{42,44,47}. Containers restarting with jitted-kernel error and then CUDA OOM at startup.

Ben_runtime: copy of container STDERR: ```
2026-02-20T02:13:03Z runtime: kvcache init failed: rdma_reorder_timeout
2026-02-20T02:13:04Z cuda: cuCtxCreate failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
2026-02-20T02:13:04Z serving: OOM allocating 512MiB for attention_kvcache
```
Repro: heavy burst of small requests to short-seq chat endpoints. We have continuous-batching turned on.

Carla_infra: I pulled node-level counters: ifconfig shows NIC flaps on mlx5_0 (carrier: off->on ~every 6s) and the RDMA layer reports pkey violations on one port. Looks like link microbursts.

Dave_oncall: immediate mitigation options? Reduced serving capacity -> customer impact.

Alice_sre: Mitigations: 1) disable cross-node K/V cache to avoid RDMA traffic (temporary) 2) scale down/bounce affected pods to cold-start on local-only mode 3) route traffic to dedicated fallback model instance in us-east. Which is fastest?

Ben_runtime: #1 we can flip a config flag in the configmap, but pods pick it up on restart. Command to patch: ```
kubectl -n serve patch cm runtime-config --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/kvstore/rdma_enabled","value":false}]'
```
Then rollout restart deployment/serve-v2. That will prevent RDMA kv exchanges and reduce IB load.

Carla_infra: While that happens, I'll cordon the two flapping nodes and reprovision a hot spare. ```
kubectl cordon node/edge-usw-node-42
kubectl drain node/edge-usw-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Note: draining will trigger restarts of the runtime pods.

Ellie_support: Support ticket triage: customers seeing 5xx rate ~4-7% in us-west for chat endpoints. Top impacted customer: AcmeCorp (tenant acme-prod) - intermittent request failures and trailing latency. I'm notifying account team.

Dave_oncall: Ok do the cm patch + rolling restart. Alice, Ben, coordinate the restart ordering so we don't bring up all pods at once and slam the fabric. Use --max-unavailable=1.

Alice_sre: Doing patch now. Applying small rate-limiter on admission to smooth burst: ```
kubectl -n serve patch deploy serve-v2 --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/cpu","value":"2000m"}]' --patch-type=merge
```  (this is a quick throttle to reduce simultaneous batch windows)

Ben_runtime: Rolling restart with maxUnavailable=1 started. Watching logs.

ops-bot: Deploy started by ben_runtime: rollout restart deployment/serve-v2 — strategy maxUnavailable=1. CI pipeline id: #5623.

Alice_sre: After first few restarts kernel logs show fewer gdr resets. rdma_rx_err rate dropping. But one node still hitting CUDA OOM on init because NV driver sees stale MMAP. I'm going to increase the device reset backoff to avoid rapid restarts.

Carla_infra: I also flushed mlx5 firmware counters and applied suspected hotfix (mlx5 reset quirk) on the flapping NICs. Running: ```
echo 1 > /sys/class/net/ib0/device/reset
rdma link status ib0
```
We see link stabilized for ~45s then small burst again. Ordering the cordon/drain seemed to reduce cross-node chatter.

Ellie_support: Update for AcmeCorp: partial mitigation in place, some requests restored. ETA for full restore unknown. Customer notified about degraded performance.

Dave_oncall: Monitoring metrics: errors per min down from 120 -> 14. P95 latency remains high ~1.1s for a bit. Please record the exact timeline for postmortem.

Alice_sre: Captured tcpdump sample and ibstat output, uploaded to /var/ops/incidents/2934012000/ for analysis. Collected kernel oops and dmesg from affected nodes.

Ben_runtime: We also toggled continuous-batching to conservative (batch size cap 8) to reduce memory pressure: ```
PATCH /runtime/config {"batching":{"max_batch_size":8}}
```
That reduced OOMs during warmup.

Carla_infra: I've removed the flapping NIC from fabric routing for now and replaced it with spare. New route uses ib1 which shows stable counters. Will keep infra in fallback mode until we confirm firmware fix.

Ellie_support: Customer impact summary draft: 2026-02-20 02:13-02:38 UTC, AcmeCorp and ~12 tenants saw elevated 5xx (avg 4.6%). No data loss. Primary cause: RDMA microburst causing link flaps + subsequent CUDA init failures on restart. Next steps: postmortem, compensatory credits?

Dave_oncall: Do we need to page infra lead for firmware rollback?

Carla_infra: cc @carla_infra: planning to coordinate with vendor tomorrow for firmware patch; for now nodes on spare NICs. Will attach firmware versions to ticket.

Ben_runtime: Suggestion for permanent mitigation: disable cross-node RDMA for small-sequence chat model traffic and prefer local-only K/V cache for microburst-prone racks. Also add backoff jitter to container restarts to avoid thundering herd on NV init.

Alice_sre: Agree. I'll draft actions and assign owners in the incident doc. Starting postmortem skeleton at https://ops.internal/pm/2934012000.

Dave_oncall: Thanks team. Setting status -> mitigated. Leaving handoff for oncall tomorrow for long-tail verification. :white_check_mark:
